name: Inspect
summary: Reads an outside agent, plugin or skill on GitHub, without running any of it, and reports what it does and how safe it is.
does: Inspect reads an outside agent's code, or a plugin or skill for a person's coding tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others), in a public GitHub repository, at its newest commit or one you name, without running any of it, and hands back an inspection report on what it does and how safe it is: a list of findings in eight sections, each citing a file and line at the commit. For a plugin it says what it adds to the person's tools, what each hook runs on their machine, what each MCP server reaches, and its risks. It also says how tied the agent is to its platform: what it uses of it, how open each part is, and, for each other platform, what moving it would take, what it would lose and what replaces each part, from AgentMesh's agent platforms database, with no recommendation. Scripts read the code by rule; a model writes only the judgments, and each judgment cites the lines it rests on. It gives no verdict on bringing it in and judges no fit with anyone's plan.

offerings.name: Inspect a repository
offerings.does: Inspects one public GitHub repository (an agent, a plugin or skills), at its newest commit or one you name, and hands back the inspection report, a copy of it to read, the dependency list and a short summary.

inputs.name: repository
inputs.about: The public GitHub repository's address, such as https://github.com/langchain-ai/design-agent.

inputs.name: commit
inputs.about: The commit to inspect, such as 86d8f66; left blank, Inspect reads the newest commit.

inputs.name: plugin
inputs.about: When the repository holds several plugins, the one to inspect, by its name; left blank, Inspect inspects the first and lists the others.

outputs.name: sbom
outputs.about: The dependency list as a CycloneDX 1.5 bill of materials, made by rule and never by the model: every component with its version, its package URL and where it was read.

outputs.name: inspection
outputs.about: The inspection report in the inspection-report-v1 format: the repository and commit, what was inspected (an agent's report says nothing more; a plugin's or skills' report says what it is, the tools it installs into, and the plugins the repository holds), the eight sections, the findings in section order, how tied it is to its platform and what moving it elsewhere would take (portability, from AgentMesh's agent platforms database), the judgments held back with why, the facts the findings cite, and what the job used. While the job runs, a working copy of it with the findings so far is posted under the same name, marked partial.

partial.description: only on the working copy posted while the job runs, never on the delivered report: the stage the job is at, how many findings so far, how many are left out of this copy to keep it one piece, and whether their words are

subject.description: 0.5.0: what a plugin or skill repository is; absent from an agent's report. kind plugin or skills; the plugin's name, version and maker as its manifests give them; the tools it installs into (tools, the main ones; also_for, the others); how many skills it has; and, for a repository of several plugins, each one with whether it is the one inspected (picked_by: the request or the first)

sha.description: the commit's full digest; null only in the first working copy, posted before GitHub's record names the commit

checked.description: true when the archive's own header named this digest

portability.description: 0.6.0: how tied it is to its platform and what moving it would take, read by rule from AgentMesh's agent platforms database, a copy pinned to one AgentMesh commit. database: the copy read, its AgentMesh commit and the date its entries were checked. built_on: the platforms the code shows, the one with the most categories first, each with the places that show it (for a plugin or skills, also the tools it runs in). uses: one row for each category the code uses, never one a platform merely offers, each with its sources (the platform's feature or the open standard, in the database's own words, how open it is, and every place in the code that shows it), whether it is an outside service, how it moves by rule (an open standard, open source that comes with its code, settings only, its code in one file or in several, its runtime, or its tool's own format) and, for an outside service, what it really needs and what the code already offers in its place, in the model's checked words. not_used and not_applicable: the categories it does not use, or that do not apply to a plugin or skills. destinations: every other platform, the first three shown (AgentMesh, then the two that keep the most of what it uses, in its language), each with the work to move it (the outside services to swap, and its own code to re-host on the destination's deployment, in the database's words) and the destination's own rating and words for each category it uses. It gives no recommendation. The working copy carries it without the evidence, and without the destinations' words when it is short of room (words_left_out).

screening_requests.description: requests to AgentMesh's screening, which passes every line before the model reads it

screening_held.description: passages the screening held, which the model did not read

text.description: the line exactly as written at the commit, when it is at most 400 characters

long_line.description: the line's length, given instead of its text when it is longer than 400 characters

call.description: the read-only call the fact came from, such as GET /repos/{owner}/{name}

level_by.description: who set the level: the record it came from (OSV), a fixed rule of Inspect's (a committed credential is high), or the model

detail.description: fields of the finding's kind: a skill's name, path, description, scripts and lift_out (yes or no) with the imports that keep it from standing alone, its size (scripts, lines of code, the length of its instructions and the tests that name it) and its instructions as text (instructions, up to 8,000 characters each and 250,000 in all; instructions_cut when shortened, with instructions_address, the file at the commit on GitHub); the agent's own code's files and lines; a job's does; a risk's safe, how to make it safe; a model's name, where it is chosen and whether a setting changes it; a system's name, host, access (read, write, read-write or unknown), the credentials it expects, need (required, optional, unclear, or none when the person has nothing to set up), supply (what the person supplies), without (what happens without it) and sends (what goes to it); since 0.4.0 need is decided by rule from the settings it reads and where the code that reaches it is (need_by rule, with need_why and need_settings), and the model's own answer stands only where they leave it unclear (need_by model), kept as need_by_model either way; a credential's need, need_by and need_why by the same rule; a tool's name, what it does and whether it runs without a person's OK; a vulnerability's package, version, OSV id, aliases and fixed version; 0.5.0: a plugin's command, sub-agent or rule its name, description, the tools it works in and may use (shell when one runs shell commands), its size (characters and lines of instructions) and its instructions; an MCP server its transport, whether it runs on the machine (local), the host it connects to, the package it fetches and whether that is pinned, how it signs in, the settings it names and what the person supplies; a hook's risk its hook (event, trigger in words, type, tools, how many hooks, what it runs, lines and files, the hosts its code calls, what it touches, why its level, and the model's words for what it does)

FindingSoFar.description: a finding in the working copy: its id, place, title and level, the first place it cites, the fields of its detail the view draws, and its words where they fit

level_by.description: who set the level: the record it came from (OSV), a fixed rule of Inspect's (a committed credential is high), or the model

more_evidence.description: how many more places the finding cites in the delivered report

detail.description: the fields of the finding's detail the view draws while the job runs (0.4.0): what was inspected, a skill's size, the agent's own code, the count of tests, a system's need and what the person supplies, a credential's need, a risk's fix; left out when the copy does not fit

outputs.name: inspection-md
outputs.about: The same report as Markdown, for a person to read: `# Inspection of <repository>`, then `## At a glance`, then `## <section title>` for sections 2 to 8, with `## Could it move?` after Systems it uses, one line per finding with its level in words, its category in words and its file and line at the commit, and no finding code.

example.good_result: A report in eight sections on what the agent does and how safe it is, each finding citing a file and line at that commit, with its risks rated by level, and how tied it is to its platform, with what moving it to each other platform would take.

refusals:
Running, installing, building or testing the repository's code, because Inspect only reads it; it says so and inspects without running anything.
Giving a verdict on whether to bring the agent in, or judging how it fits a plan or a catalog role, because that decision is the reader's; it says so and still delivers the report.
A branch or a tag in place of a commit, because a branch or a tag can move and the report must stand for one commit; it asks for the commit's digest, or for the commit to be left blank so it reads the newest one, and inspects nothing.
A plugin the request names that the repository does not hold, or one it lists but keeps in another repository, because there is nothing of it here to read; it names the plugins the repository holds, or where that one is kept, and inspects nothing.
A repository that is not public on GitHub, or a commit that is not in it, because there is nothing it may read; it says which, and inspects nothing.
An archive larger than 50 MB or holding more than 20000 files, because it reads no more than that; it says how large the archive is, and inspects nothing.
Writing a link from the archive, or a file whose path leaves its own folder, because an archive from somebody else must not decide where a file lands; it records each one as a fact and writes neither.
Repeating the characters of anything that looks like a committed credential, because a report that repeats a key has published it; it keeps only the file, the line and the kind of credential.
Asking for more than 20 inspections in a day as one asker, or after 200 have started that day, because each inspection asks a model for its judgments and the day is bounded; it says when to try again, and inspects nothing.
Judging text from the repository that AgentMesh's screening has not passed, because a repository can be written to steer the model that reads it; a passage the screening holds is left out of what the model reads and named as a risk, and when the screening cannot answer, the report holds no judgment and says why.

records.name: the signed job manifest of each delivery

systems.name: code-host
systems.needs: To read the public repository's record, the commit's record, its recent commits and the archive of the repository at the commit from api.github.com, with GET requests only and no key.

systems.name: vulnerability-database
systems.needs: To ask api.osv.dev which exact versions of the dependencies have known vulnerabilities, by queries that change nothing, and to read the record of each one found.

systems.name: text-reasoning
systems.needs: To write the judgments over the facts the scripts found: what the agent does, how it works, what it can do on its own, its risks and what it needs to run safely, and the few findings that matter most. Every line it is given has passed AgentMesh's screening first.

can_use.does: writes the organization's name as the brand writes it, uses its first-mention form the first time, and keeps out the words the brand never says; and draws in the brand's colors and faces and places its mark
can_use.without: writes the organization's name as the person gave it, and says that no brand profile was given; and draws in this agent's own plain house style, and says that no brand profile was given

can_use.does: writes in the organization's voice, tone and spelling, and uses the words it prefers in place of the ones it avoids
can_use.without: writes in a plain, neutral voice in the spelling of the words it was given, and says that no style guide was given
